articles.body: Hardik Pandya’s prolonged absence from competitive cricket has once again brought the issue of player workload, game time and injuries into focus, with India also dealing with fitness concerns involving several other players.Pandya has not played competitive cricket since the final week of IPL 2026. He was expected to return for India A in the upcoming ODI series against Australia A, beginning October 6, but his comeback was delayed. His return-to-play date had been set for September 20, and he is now ruled out of the upcoming white-ball tour of New Zealand.So what does Pandya need to do to be available more often?“Play more cricket,” former India captain Kapil Dev told Times of India.Asked if he felt Pandya was not doing that, Kapil said: “I don’t know. You play more, your body gets tuned to that. But if you play less and suddenly you play more, chances of injury increase. If your muscles are fine, your injuries are less.”Kapil’s comments come at a time when India are dealing with a number of injury concerns. Prasidh Krishna has been ruled out for at least three weeks and is highly likely to miss the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand. India’s tour of New Zealand begins with the T20I series on October 22.Harshit Rana has also suffered a fitness setback and is unlikely to be picked for India’s upcoming tour of New Zealand. Rana was ruled out of the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan as well as the 2026 Asian Games last month due to injury. He was recovering at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru but developed low-grade pain in his left quadriceps during a match simulation.Pandya, meanwhile, has been away from competitive cricket since the conclusion of IPL 2026, while Harshit last featured during India’s white-ball leg against England in July.The wider spread of cricket injuries over the last four-five years also prompted a discussion with Kapil on whether the volume of cricket has contributed to the problem.The former India captain pointed to the difference in the playing patterns of his generation, citing Sandeep Patil’s observation about how players used to remain involved in different forms of domestic cricket.“Sandeep Patil put it very nicely. ‘In our time we used to play Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, club cricket, other cricket too.’ In 365 days, if you can play 250 days, you’re in the game.”For Kapil, regular cricket helps the body stay accustomed to the demands of the game. articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already generated enormous excitement around Indian cricket, but former India captain Kapil Dev believes it is far too early to
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already generated enormous excitement around Indian cricket, but former India captain Kapil Dev believes it is far too early to judge whether the teenage sensation can go on to become the next big name in the game.At 15, Sooryavanshi has already made a significant impact at the age-group, India A, IPL and is now part of India’s T20I setup. But with the youngster currently waiting for his opportunity behind the established opening pair of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson, Kapil believes there is little value in rushing to make predictions about his future.“It’s too early. Does he have the ability? Yes. But there have been so many in cricket who came with so much ability, then faded out,” Kapil told Times of India.Kapil cited former India batter Vinod Kambli as an example of a player whose immense talent did not translate into the kind of long-term career many expected.“Look at Vinod Kambli. What we will say about that?” he said.Sooryavanshi, who is still only 15, has plenty of time on his side. Kapil believes the next few years will be more revealing than his current performances.“Vaibhav is 15 years old. Give him another three years, then we will talk. When his lifestyle changes, his thinking too will change. Then we’ll come to know how he will look after the next two years. That is more important than looking at his performance,” Kapil said.The teenager has already given Indian cricket plenty to talk about. In June, in his last innings as an uncapped player, Sooryavanshi smashed the fastest fifty in List A cricket, reaching the milestone in just 11 balls before finishing with 94 off 29 balls for India A in the tri-series final against Sri Lanka A.Earlier in February, he produced another remarkable performance in the Under-19 World Cup final in Harare, smashing 175 off 80 balls to help India Under-19 win the title. His IPL career also began with a bang, In 2026 season he broke several batting records this year and won the Orange Cap before being blooded into India’s T20I side.But Kapil’s broader view of young cricketers is not about one innings or one season. He said he is always looking for players who can potentially stay at the top level for a decade or more.“Any young cricketer who we can feel has a future for the next 10 years, 15 years. Those type of cricketers. We have seen Rohit, Virat. We already saw Sachin. And they made us so proud,” Kapil told Times of India.“But you’re always looking for the next hero. You always ask, ‘Who is the next hero?’ As a cricketer I like to see which is that young boy who has got that chance, who can replace Virat Kohli. And play for 15 years. That’s what my mind looks for.”For Sooryavanshi, the attention is unlikely to disappear anytime soon. But Kapil’s message is clear: talent can open the door, but how a teenager develops away from the spotlight may ultimately determine how long he stays at the top.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: From MI family to CSK: Kieron Pollard's complete T20 franchise journey across tournaments detailed
articles.summary: Pollard's T20 journey spans the world's biggest franchise leagues, from Mumbai Indians to Joburg Super Kings.
articles.body:
Kieron Pollard's move to Joburg Super Kings for SA20 2027 ends his long association with the Mumbai Indians family.

The West Indies great has played across the IPL , CPL , PSL, BBL, BPL, ILT20, MLC, SA20 and The Hundred .

Pollard played only for Mumbai Indians in the IPL before retiring in 2022 and becoming their batting coach.

He could now face an MI-owned team in the SA20, though he will not return to the IPL as a player.

Kieron Pollard's journey from Mumbai Indians to Joburg Super Kings

Kieron Pollard and the Mumbai Indians have had one of the longest-standing relationships in franchise cricket. In the IPL and the various other global T20 tournaments, the former all-rounder from West Indies became one of the key figures for MI. The duo went on to win various titles under MI.

However, the partnership took an unexpected turn in the 2027 SA20 season when Joburg Super Kings bought Pollard at the auction for R1.5 million. Thus, the Super Kings have brought on board Pollard, who was previously a member of MI Cape Town, adding another interesting chapter to the life of a player who has traveled across T20 leagues globally.

Pollard's stint as a member of different franchises goes way back from the IPL. He has played for franchises in the Caribbean Premier League and Australia's Big Bash League, as well as in various other places, including Pakistan, Bangladesh, the UAE, the United States, and England.

Kieron Pollard's complete T20 franchise journey: List of teams

Pollard has represented franchises across several major T20 leagues during his career. His latest move came at the SA20 2027 auction, when Joburg Super Kings signed him for R1.5 million, ending his association with MI Cape Town.

Mumbai Indians: The franchise that defined Pollard's IPL career

Pollard played for Mumbai Indians in IPL from 2010, and his stint with the franchise spanned 13 seasons. He scored 3,412 runs and took 69 wickets in the tournament.

Furthermore, Pollard featured in five successful IPL title wins for the franchise and also participated in Mumbai's Champions League T20 successes in 2011 and 2013.

The association with MI continued even when he retired as a player in November 2022. Instead of switching teams in the IPL, Pollard became the batting coach of the side while playing for the franchise's teams in overseas leagues.

These included MI Emirates in ILT20, MI New York in MLC, and MI Cape Town in the SA20. Pollard joining Joburg Super Kings team is thus a significant breakaway from the network of franchises that he had been associated with over his entire career.

Why Pollard's move to Joburg Super Kings is significant

What makes the signing even more impressive is the fact that Chennai Super Kings tried to get Pollard in the 2010 IPL auction; however, their efforts were defeated by Mumbai Indians. Over 16 years later, Pollard will play for the brand Chennai Super Kings in the SA20, but he won't be playing for the CSK in the IPL.

The signing is even more interesting because Joburg Super Kings and MI Cape Town are part of rival franchise groups. This means Pollard could have faced the very team he played with in the South African tournament.

The signing does not wipe out Pollard's past with the Mumbai Indians. It simply provides him with an opportunity to continue his career in a different franchise group.

Pollard versus MI in the SA20 could be a fascinating subplot

Pollard will not face the Mumbai Indians directly in the IPL as he has retired from playing and is still with them as batting coach. The situation becomes more intriguing in the SA20 league, where Pollard is set to play for Joburg Super Kings against his former MI side in MI Cape Town.

Just as Pollard will be well aware of his previous SA20 side's players and culture, MI Cape Town will also be aware of the capabilities of the strong Caribbean batter in crunch moments.

It is not a traditional franchise move but a very intriguing one, as Pollard will have his association with Mumbai, whereas with Joburg Super Kings, he might give one of the best individual confrontations in the SA20.

articles.title: Sandpapergate: 2018 ball-tampering scandal explained as Australia return to South Africa for Test cricket
articles.summary: What was 'Sandpapergate', who was involved and what were the punishments? Ball-tampering scandal from 2018 in focus as Australia return to South Africa for Test series for first time since; watch live on Sky Sports Cricket from 7.30am Friday (8.30am first ball)
articles.body:
For the first time since 'Sandpapergate', which resulted in Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft receiving bans for the roles they played in the plot to alter the condition of the ball, Australia are preparing for a Test series in South Africa.

Ahead of the first Test in Durban from Friday, live on Sky Sports from 7.30am (8.30am first ball) , here is an explainer of what transpired in Cape Town and its subsequent fallout…

That was the name given to the March 2018 ball-tampering scandal during Australia's Test tour of South Africa after Bancroft was caught on camera trying to rough up one side of the ball with sandpaper in order the make it swing through the air.

The incident occurred on day three of the third Test in Cape Town while South Africa were batting in their second innings, with Bancroft aiming to hide the sandpaper, which he initially said was a piece of tape, in his trousers after realising he had been spotted.

At the end of the day's play, Bancroft and Australia captain Smith admitted to ball-tampering in a press conference - albeit not to the use of sandpaper at that stage - with Smith saying the plan had been cooked up by the 'leadership group' at lunch.

Smith and vice-captain Warner stood down from their leadership roles for the remainder of the Cape Town Test but still took to the field as the Baggy Greens, now captained by Tim Paine, slumped to a 322-run defeat after being rolled for just 107 in their second innings - Warner top-scoring with 32, Bancroft making 26 and Smith seven.

Smith, Warner and Bancroft were sent home ahead of the fourth Test, in which Australia were hammered by 492 runs to fall to a 3-1 series defeat, and later received hefty bans from international and domestic cricket, ranging from nine months to a year.

They were each found by Cricket Australia to have engaged in conduct against the spirit of the game and harmful to its interests.

Warner was found to have led the plot to alter the condition of the ball, including guiding Bancroft on how to use the sandpaper.

He was slapped with a one-year ban and told he would never be considered for a leadership position within the team again.

Smith - who would go on to be succeeded permanently by Paine as captain - was also suspended for 12 months after failing to prevent a plan he was aware of and making misleading comments.

He was also informed he would not be able to take a leadership role until at least 12 months after the conclusion of his ban.

Smith and Warner were removed from the 2018 IPL, where they were due to play for - and initially captain - Rajasthan Royals and SunRisers Hyderabad respectively, while Bancroft saw Somerset cancel the deal he had signed to play county cricket.

Australia coach Darren Lehmann was among the collateral damage.

Lehmann - now coaching Northamptonshire in county cricket, leading the Steelbacks to the 2026 T20 Blast title - was cleared of any involvement in the ball-tampering scandal but opted to resign after the fourth and final Test against South Africa.

Without Smith, Warner and Bancroft, Australia would go on to lose Test series away to Pakistan and at home to India, before a 2-0 win in Sri Lanka preceded their comeback series - the 2-2 Ashes draw in England in the summer of 2019.

Some argued that the sanctions meted out were too severe, including former India internationals Gautam Gambhir and Harbhajan Singh and broadcaster and ex-Hampshire captain Mark Nicholas - a view shared by the late, great Shane Warne.

Leg-spin legend Warne, who died in 2022, said while it was "embarrassing" for Australia to be caught up in the scandal, he felt worldwide "hysteria" led to a punishment "not fitting the crime".

Smith and Bancroft gave emotional press conferences on their returns to Australia after being sent home, while Bancroft later admitted he had considered quitting and becoming a yoga teacher during his enforced break from the game.

While all three players went on to represent Australia again - Smith is still doing so - Bancroft's international career arguably never truly recovered with the opener's two Tests at the start of the 2019 Ashes his, at this point, last international matches.

Warner, who retired from internationals in 2024, applied to have his lifetime captaincy ban lifted but then revoked that in 2022.

The suspension was ultimately lifted and he went on to lead Sydney Thunder in the Big Bash League.

How does Smith reflect on 'Sandpapergate'?

Speaking to News Corp recently, Smith said: "That was a traumatic experience in my life and when I hear the flash of a camera it makes me revisit that, in a way.

"The 24-48 hours after being told I was getting banned for a year, going through the airport in Johannesburg getting absolutely mobbed, and then flying back and doing a press conference... I still have little flashbacks here and there of it.

"I felt like I was kind of thrown to the wolves through [Johannesburg] airport. I didn't have any support there at all.

"It was certainly a difficult period, particularly the initial few days after. The mental state I was in was not great.

"That's somewhere I'd like not to get to again, but I certainly learned from that and have been able to move forward with my life.

"I've tried to kind of erase a lot of 2018 and what happened. I can't remember a lot about the series. I've tried to block most of it out of my memory bank."

What reactions can Australia expect in South Africa?

Australia have returned to South Africa since 'Sandpapergate' but only for white-ball cricket with a proposed Test tour in 2021 cancelled due to Covid-19.

England fans regularly teased their Ashes rivals after the ball-tampering scandal, with some dressing up as sandpaper to make their point, so what sort of response can Smith and the current players expects from South Africa supporters?

Former Proteas all-rounder Shaun Pollock told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast : "I don't think it'll be overly hostile.

"Over here, there's been quite a few replays of the [2018] series over the last few weeks, just to create a bit of animosity, I suppose, but when you play against Australia, people in South Africa won't need a reason to have a go at them about some particular reason.

"I'm sure there'll be a few people coming dressed up in accordance with 'Sandpapergate', I'm sure there'll be some continual reminding of it, but I don't think it'll be over the top or too intense."

Finally, is there any more to come out over 'Sandpapergate'?

While Cricket Australia found only Warner, Smith and Bancroft were party to the plot, Bancroft said in an interview in 2021 that it was "self-explanatory" bowlers in the team had to be aware the ball was being meddled with.

Cricket Australia said they were open to investigating any new information brought to light.

The whole episode is one Australia will want to forget but will likely never be allowed to.

articles.summary: Mohammed Shami could soon find his way back into the India squad, according to former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin, who believes the change in the
articles.body: Mohammed Shami could soon find his way back into the India squad, according to former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin, who believes the change in the selection setup may open the door for the veteran pacer.India recently announced their squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, which follows the ongoing T20I series against the West Indies. The biggest talking point from the selection was the return of Bhuvneshwar Kumar to the national side after a four-year absence.The squad was also the first selected after Ajit Agarkar completed his stint as chief selector. With Agarkar no longer part of the setup, Ashwin feels India could be moving towards a greater reliance on experience, particularly with Jasprit Bumrah's workload being managed regularly.Speaking on his YouTube channel Ash Ki Baat, Ashwin suggested that the change in approach could benefit Shami as well."The chairman of selectors is set to be changed. Ajit Agarkar is no longer a part of the setup. Maybe Ajit focused more on youngsters and newcomers. But now you see, without Bumrah, India's bowling attack can be a little susceptible. The BCCI is now leaning towards experience. The fact that they have picked Bhuvneshwar (Kumar), I wouldn't say that the door is shut on (Mohammed) Shami either. But I am extremely happy that Bhuvneshwar has broken down the door for his selection," Ashwin said.Shami last represented India in the Champions Trophy 2025 final against New Zealand in March last year. Since then, the pacer has not been selected to play for India in any format.His absence from the national side had also led to repeated exchanges between Shami and Agarkar over his non-selection. Agarkar had previously indicated that Shami was not fully fit, but the pacer showcased his fitness by playing domestic cricket and regularly picking up wickets.The 35-year-old has an extensive international record, having played 64 Tests, 108 ODIs and 25 T20Is for India. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sanju Samson’s poor run is the only concern for India’s otherwise strong batting line-up as they prepare for the second T20I against West Indies on Friday.India can take a 2-0 lead in the five-match series with another win, but the team management could consider making a change at the top of the order after Samson’s recent struggles.Samson under pressureSamson has managed only 9, 7, 2 and 11 in his last four innings. His partnerships in those games have also produced little, with stands of 7, 12, 2 and 29. The Kerala batter has had opportunities, but has not been able to convert them into a substantial score. That could make the management think about giving young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi another chance alongside Abhishek Sharma at the top.Sooryavanshi waiting for another chanceSooryavanshi has impressed whenever he has been given an opportunity in T20 cricket. The teenager has shown a wide range of shots and the confidence to take on bowlers from the start.His ability to change the course of a game has made him an attractive option for India. However, the team has so far preferred the established opening combination of Abhishek and Samson.Shreyas Iyer’s form has also eased the pressure on the top order. The India captain has looked increasingly comfortable in the T20I role and scored his maiden century in the format in his 68th match.Mayank could make wayIndia could also make a change to their pace attack after Mayank Yadav had an expensive outing in the first T20I in Lucknow.The pacer conceded 16 runs in the opening over and continued to leak runs during the middle overs and at the death. He did, however, provide India with an important breakthrough when he dismissed West Indies’ leading scorer Sherfane Rutherford in the penultimate over.India could consider playing all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy and use him with the new ball. However, that plan did not produce the desired results during the ODI series against West Indies.Spin attack deliversIndia’s spin combination looked much more settled in the opening T20I after Kuldeep Yadav joined Axar Patel in the playing XI.Both spinners took two wickets each and kept the West Indies batters under pressure.Naman Dhir was another positive for India. articles.title: India vs West Indies in Ranchi brings back an Ajit Agarkar memory - but his role has completely changed
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ajit Agarkar will not be around the selection table when India take on West Indies in the second T20I at the JSCA International Stadium Complex
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ajit Agarkar will not be around the selection table when India take on West Indies in the second T20I at the JSCA International Stadium Complex on Friday. But the former India pacer has an interesting connection with Ranchi and the venue.The last time Ranchi hosted a T20I, Agarkar was there too - not as the chairman of the BCCI selection committee, but as a pitch expert.In 2023, when India played New Zealand in a T20I at the same venue, Agarkar did the pitch report before the match.As part of the broadcast coverage, Agarkar assessed the playing conditions and pointed out the dimensions of the ground, the grass cover and the possible impact of dew."The average first innings score is 156. Square boundaries are little over 60 and straight boundaries are little over 70, in the corner around the players pavilion it's only 57 and 59 metres. The pitch looks excellent, there is even covering of grass and there might be some help with the new ball. There is a lot of talk about the dew, the curator kept the grass as minimum as possible on the outfield to negate the dew factor. The ball will skid on nicely, but looks an excellent pitch for batting," reckon Ajit Agarkar in 2023.Three years later, as India return to Ranchi for another T20I, Agarkar’s tenure as chairman of selectors has come to an end.Agarkar’s three-year stint endsThe BCCI invited applications on Tuesday to fill the vacant position in the men’s selection committee following Agarkar’s exit. Agarkar’s tenure ended on October 4. The former India pacer had informed the board after its Annual General Meeting on September 18 that he would not seek an extension.Pragyan Ojha is currently the interim chairman of selectors, with Shiv Sundar Das, Ajay Ratra and RP Singh the other members of the panel.“The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) invites applications for one position on its Men's Selection Committee," the BCCI said on its website.The deadline for applications is October 14.BCCI thanks AgarkarAgarkar leaves the post after a successful period for Indian cricket. During his tenure, India won the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups and the 2025 Champions Trophy. The team also won two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games gold medals, while reaching the 2023 ODI World Cup final. His tenure also saw the beginning of a major transition in Indian cricket, with Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma retiring from T20Is and Tests.The BCCI thanked Agarkar for his contribution and highlighted the major achievements during his time as chairman.“A tenure marked by some truly special moments for Indian cricket — three ICC trophies, two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games Gold medals, along with a run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final,” the BCCI posted on its official X account.“Thank you, Mr Ajit Agarkar for your commitment, conviction and contribution as Chairman of the Men’s Selection Committee. Wishing you the very best for the journey ahead,” the board added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Six hours a day, 19% to 14% body fat: Inside Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s bid for longevity at 36
articles.summary: On November 22, 2022, Bhuvneshwar Kumar played his last match for India, against New Zealand.
articles.body: On November 22, 2022, Bhuvneshwar Kumar played his last match for India, against New Zealand. Four years later, he has returned to the Indian T20I squad against the same opposition.The recall came on earlier this week, when the BCCI announced India's squad for the five-match T20I series in New Zealand. The 36-year-old’s name was one of the biggest talking points in the 16-member squad.In between were four years without an India call-up, a shift from international regular to domestic leader, and a fitness routine that, according to the man who has worked closely with him, demanded hours every day.A few months before his return, he had taken 28 wickets in 16 matches for Royal Challengers Bengaluru in IPL 2026, finishing as the joint-highest wicket-taker of the season. His wickets came at an average of 17.89 and an economy rate of 7.95 as RCB won their second successive IPL title.After the IPL, Bhuvneshwar captained Lucknow Falcons in the UPT20 league to the final, taking 14 wickets in 11 matches at 16.57, with an economy rate of 6.82.The work away from the cricket fieldAfter RCB made it to their back-to-back final of IPL, TimesofIndia.com spoke to Bhuvneshwar's personal strength and conditioning coach, Surya Pratap Yadav, about the changes behind the scenes.One of the biggest areas of focus was body composition. “Our primary focus has been reducing body fat while increasing muscle mass. As athletes age, muscle loss becomes a concern, so we worked extensively on strength training, protein intake, and supplementation.“Bhuvneshwar's body fat percentage has come down from 19% to 14%, while maintaining his weight, which indicates muscle gain. His strength levels have improved significantly, and that has helped increase force production and running speed,” Surya Pratap had told TimesofIndia.com in May this year.“Discipline is the biggest factor. He understands his body's weak points and works on them proactively. We dedicate nearly an hour every day to rehab and injury-prevention exercises. Along with that, we focus heavily on recovery, hydration, sleep, protein intake, and supplements. All of these factors help him stay fit throughout the season,” added Pratap.Then there is the volume of work.“A lot more than people realise, he spends 6-7 hours a day training. That includes gym sessions, rehabilitation work, recovery routines, batting practice, bowling practice, and training in different environments. Even if it isn't always visible on social media, the amount of effort he puts in every day is tremendous,” Surya Pratap Yadav had said.For a fast bowler in his mid-30s, that workload has to be managed as carefully as the bowling itself. Bhuvneshwar's answer was to make the routine part of his cricket life rather than something reserved for a comeback attempt.From India regular to domestic workhorseThe years after his India exit were not spent away from competitive cricket. Bhuvneshwar remained a key figure for Uttar Pradesh in domestic cricket, leading the bowling attack in competitions including the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy and Vijay Hazare Trophy. The IPL remained another constant.He had already stopped attaching his daily work to the expectation of a national recall, but the grind continued. In a video posted by RCB, Bhuvneshwar explained why he had stopped setting long-term targets.“I am not thinking about India’s comeback. It has been many years since I stopped keeping or making long-term goals because whenever I did that, it never worked for me. I am happy that I have played 200 matches and taken so many wickets in the powerplay and at the death. I think it is all a reward for what I have done over the years.Bhuvneshwar Kumar after his last India appearanceSeasonCompetitionMatchesWicketsAverageEconomyBest2023Vijay Hazare Trophy111116.904.964/202023Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy7169.315.845/162023UP T20 League91415.365.813/112023-24Ranji Trophy21313.532.838/412024IPL161148.459.352/122024UP T20 League11731. 856.282/222024-25Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy91116.006.033/62025IPL141728.419.293/332025UP T20 League101417.006.704/122025-26Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy7819.257.003/232026IPL162817.897.954/232026UP T20 League111416.576.824/10The skill that still gives him a route backBhuvneshwar's return for the NZ series also puts his bowling in a wider context. He has long been one of India's most effective swing bowlers, particularly when the new ball offers movement. His overseas record has included strong spells in England, the West Indies, South Africa and other conditions where the ability to move the ball in the air remains valuable.However, his returns in New Zealand have been modest - having taken 15 wickets in 15 matches, with an average of 38.00. His numbers on the last New Zealand trip: four wickets in five T20Is at an average of 40.00 and an economy rate of 8.42.But the relevance of Bhuvneshwar's return is not confined to the numbers from one series. articles.title: Dhananjaya de Silva steps down as Sri Lanka Test captain
articles.summary: Dhananjaya de Silva has stepped down as Sri Lanka’s Test captain with immediate effect, bringing an end to his stint as skipper after 18 matches.
articles.body: Dhananjaya de Silva has stepped down as Sri Lanka’s Test captain with immediate effect, bringing an end to his stint as skipper after 18 matches. The 35-year-old will, however, continue to make himself available for selection as a player.De Silva informed the Sri Lanka Cricket Board’s selection committee of his decision in a letter, saying he believes the leadership should now be handed over to the next generation.“It’s my genuine opinion that the mantle should go down to the next generation,” de Silva said in the letter.De Silva took over as Sri Lanka’s Test captain in January 2024 after Dimuth Karunaratne retired. During his 18 Tests in charge between 2024 and 2026, Sri Lanka won seven matches, lost eight and drew three.His tenure included series victories against Afghanistan at home, Bangladesh both at home and away, and New Zealand at home.One of his standout performances as captain came in only his second Test in charge, when he scored centuries in both innings in Sylhet to help Sri Lanka secure a 328-run victory over Bangladesh. He added two more centuries during his captaincy and averaged 36.45 with the bat.De Silva’s decision comes after a difficult period for Sri Lankan cricket. The team currently sit seventh in the World Test Championship standings following a series defeat in the West Indies and a home series loss to India.De Silva, who has played 69 Tests for Sri Lanka, remains one of the most experienced members of the side.“Sri Lanka Cricket wishes him the very best for the remainder of his career and thanks him for the leadership he provided to our Test team,” SLC CEO Ashley de Silva said.Sri Lanka have yet to announce a replacement for De Silva. Their next Test assignment is a two-match series against Pakistan, beginning in Rawalpindi on November 9.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'There shouldn’t be any questions': Pujara comes out in support of Sanju Samson ahead of West Indies 2nd T20I
articles.summary: Sanju Samson may be enduring a lean run, but former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes the wicketkeeper-batter deserves something more valuable than
articles.body: Sanju Samson may be enduring a lean run, but former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes the wicketkeeper-batter deserves something more valuable than another chance, backing and security from the team management.With India leading the five-match T20I series 1-0 after an eight-wicket win over the West Indies in Lucknow, Samson's form has become one of the talking points ahead of the second T20I in Ranchi. He managed only 11 in the series opener, extending a string of low scores that also included 9, 7 and 2 during India's recent Asian Games campaign.However, Pujara feels India should resist the temptation to make changes based on a couple of failures and instead allow Samson to rediscover his rhythm.‘There shouldn’t be any questions around his place’Pujara believes Samson's pedigree and recent contributions should give him enough credit in the bank to withstand a few failures."I hope that there is no pressure on him, because there shouldn't be. He has won a World Cup for the Indian team and performed exceptionally well there. He's a quality player. So there shouldn't be any questions around him being part of the playing XI," Pujara told JioHotstar.The former India batter stressed that T20 cricket naturally comes with failures and that the team management's role becomes even more important when a player goes through a difficult phase."Yes, you might have one or two bad games, and then if he has that, that's the time when the team management has to step in, to give him the right message that, 'You are an important part of this team and will be part of this playing XI, so just go out there, express yourself, play your natural game,'" he said.Pujara also acknowledged that young batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is waiting in the wings, but believes India should not rush into making changes."And in a T20 format, there'll be some failures in between. But that's the time when you talk to a player, give him the right message. Yes, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is there, he will get his opportunity when the right time comes, but you don't make too many changes. If Sanju plays another two or three innings, I'm sure he will perform exceptionally well," he added.Pujara backs Abhishek after Lucknow setbackPujara also came to the defence of another India batter who endured a disappointing outing in the series opener, Abhishek Sharma.The explosive opener got off to a positive start against the West Indies' seamers but fell to off-spinner Roston Chase while attempting to clear the field. Pujara felt the dismissal was more a case of poor shot selection than a sign of any technical or form-related concern."Abhishek got off to a good start against seamers, but Shai Hope quickly realised that on that Lucknow pitch there was enough assistance for the spinners. Abhishek's record against off-spinners hasn't been great, though he's improved that number significantly," Pujara said.He felt Abhishek could have chosen a better option against Chase, with his attempted shot ending up in the hands of the long-off fielder."At Lucknow again, it looked like he wasn't in the best frame of mind against spinners. His options, especially against Roston Chase, could have been slightly better. He wanted to hit that ball over covers, but eventually it ended up going to long-off."‘He will be raring to go’Despite the setback, Pujara remains confident that Abhishek will bounce back quickly, pointing towards the youngster's ability to strike the ball cleanly."I'm sure he will learn this very quickly, because he's timing the ball well. The turnaround time between the games wasn't ideal, so with one game, you don't judge him too much. It was just one of those off days for him, but in the second T20I, he will be raring to go," he concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Kagiso Rabada misses out on first Test as Anrich Nortje earns surprise recall
articles.summary: Kagiso Rabada still recovering from a hamstring injury suffered in June; South Africa select two spinners for first Test and Anrich Nortje, over three years since his last first-class game; Australia also considering picking 34-year-old Nic Maddinson 10 years since his last Test cap
articles.body:
Naming their side for the series opener, which starts on Friday - live on Sky Sports Cricket from 7.30am (play starts 8.30am) - South Africa have instead opted for two spinners, Simon Harmer and Keshav Maharaj, while Anrich Nortje is a surprise selection.

Rabada trained with the team at Kingsmead on Thursday, and it's hopeful he'll still have a part to play in the second and third Tests, the first of which in Gqeberha starts on October 18.

"It ‌wasn't an easy decision," South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said on Thursday. "I think we did go the conservative route, to give him a couple ​of extra days to get closer to where he can be at 100 per cent fitness.

"Obviously for us, as ⁠soon as he gets the green ⁠light from the medical team, we expect him to be in the starting lineup."

As for the recall of 32-year-old pacer Nortje, more than three years since he last played first-class cricket, Bavuma said: "It's hard to ignore his X factor.

"There aren't many guys around who are bowling 150 (kph) plus. And I think as a batter that's not something that I ⁠would look forward to."

Bavuma added on the selection of both Harmer and Maharaj: "Those ​spin twins, if I can call them that, have added another ​dimension to our bowling attack.

"As much as we've always been about ⁠fast bowling, when conditions have allowed for spinners to come into the game they've been able to play an effective role.

"If the conditions play that way, the whole team ⁠is confident in that they can put the ​opposition under pressure. I think there's a healthy competition between them ​so that always helps."

Australia toy with controversial selection of Maddinson

Australia, still yet to name their team for the first Test, are toying with their own bold selection and the potential recall of batter Nic Maddinson.

Maddinson played three Test matches for Australia in late 2016, averaging 6.75, with his career since stalled by injury, mental health issues, and then a testicular cancer diagnosis that sidelined him for most of last year.

As a result, the 34-year-old hasn't played a first-class match since March 2025, but it was he who got the nod last week as a late addition to the touring squad due to injuries to Cameron Green and Josh Inglis.

Former Australian opener Matthew Hayden was critical of the call up, saying on the All Over Bar The Cricket podcast : "We are promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we've seen in a generation of cricket.

"And if we continue to lay that out and expect a bloke averaging 35 is going to average 55 in Test match cricket, then [selectors] George Bailey and Tony Dodemaide, you are dreaming.

"I will just put it that simply. You are frigging dreaming. You are piling up this dog s*** explanation and, in my opinion, disrespecting first-class cricket.

"You should be picking guys averaging 45 or more, and you can't, because they don't want to play. They don't want to play this version of the game.

"Mitch Marsh is a good example. He is making millions of dollars playing cricket all over the world for franchises. This is the fundamental problem we have."

articles.title: 'You can’t beat experience': Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak explains Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s India recall
articles.summary: Four years after his last appearance for India, Bhuvneshwar Kumar has once again found his way into the national T20I setup.
articles.body: Four years after his last appearance for India, Bhuvneshwar Kumar has once again found his way into the national T20I setup. At 36, the veteran pacer’s return may appear surprising on paper, but India assistant coach Sitanshu Kotak believes there is a simple explanation, experience backed by performances.Bhuvneshwar was rewarded with a recall for India’s upcoming T20I series against New Zealand after playing a pivotal role in Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s back-to-back IPL title triumphs. The pacer picked up 45 wickets across the 2025 and 2026 seasons, including 17 in 2025 and a career-best 28 in 2026.‘At some stage, you need experience’While the final call rested with the selectors, Kotak suggested that India's need for an experienced campaigner in a relatively young bowling attack could have played a significant role in Bhuvneshwar's recall."One thing is obviously with the selectors, but I can give you an answer based on what I think. In England, I personally felt that with Bumrah not being around and a lot of young bowlers playing, you can't beat experience," Kotak said during the pre-match media interaction ahead of India's second T20I against the West Indies."The young bowlers are good, they are performing well and getting selected, but at some stage you also need some experience," he added.Two seasons of IPL form opened the doorBhuvneshwar's experience alone, however, may not have been enough to earn him a return. His performances over the last two IPL seasons have strengthened his case considerably. The 36-year-old played an important role in RCB's title-winning campaigns in 2025 and 2026, claiming 17 wickets in the former before producing an even more impressive 28-wicket season in the latter.Kotak pointed to that consistency as another major factor behind the selectors' decision."Another thing is that Bhuvneshwar has been doing really well in the IPL for the last two seasons. So the selectors must have thought that, for New Zealand conditions and all, obviously he has been doing well and we need some experience," he said."They must have picked him. That's what I can think, unless you can think something different."New Zealand conditions could suit BhuviBhuvneshwar's recall also comes with India preparing for a T20I series in New Zealand, where his ability to move the new ball could prove particularly useful. articles.title: 'We've got to get into the grind': Pat Cummins urges Australia to move beyond individual brilliance
articles.summary: Australia have often thrived on explosive individual performances, but Pat Cummins wants his team to prepare for a very different kind of Test challenge
articles.body: Australia have often thrived on explosive individual performances, but Pat Cummins wants his team to prepare for a very different kind of Test challenge against South Africa: one where patience, discipline and the ability to grind out sessions could matter more than spectacular moments.With the first Test beginning at Kingsmead on Friday, Cummins acknowledged that Australia cannot always rely on a Travis Head hundred or a Mitchell Starc burst to swing matches in their favour. With conditions expected to fluctuate on a traditionally tricky Durban surface, the captain believes his side must be ready to adapt to whatever the game throws at them.‘It might not be the glamorous stuff’Australia's recent Test cricket has often been fast-paced. Their last Test against Bangladesh in August finished inside two days, while two of the five Ashes Tests against England last summer also ended within two days. Cummins feels that has meant his side has not had enough opportunities to practise grinding their way through long, attritional contests."For the batsmen and for the bowling group as well, getting into that grind is important. We haven't played too many of those kinds of Test matches in the last few years, particularly in Australia," Cummins said at his pre-match press conference."They've been quite fast-paced. A lot of our success has come off big moments, be it a Travis Head century or Starcy (fast bowler Mitchell Starc) running through the top order," he added.From big moments to sustained pressureCummins knows those match-winning bursts remain part of Australia's identity, but he wants his players to be comfortable when there are no quick breakthroughs or whirlwind innings."I think we've got to get a little bit better, and we can get a bit better getting into the grind, It might not be the glamorous stuff, but it's that grinding out of sessions, not these whirlwind innings at times. Whatever tempo gets thrown at us or what the game needs, we must make sure we match that," he said.Australia yet to finalise XIAustralia have also delayed naming their playing XI, with Cummins revealing that the selectors wanted another look at the Kingsmead surface before making the final call."We don't know our team at this stage; the selectors will come down here and we'll just want to have one more look at the ground," he said.The visitors have some selection decisions to make, particularly in the batting department. Cameron Green is unavailable, while Josh Inglis is also absent, leaving Australia to weigh up different combinations."We're trying to work out what we think is the best batting line-up for these conditions. Obviously, Cam Green's out and Josh Inglis isn't here as well," Cummins said.‘Everyone brings something different’Rather than simply replacing the missing players like-for-like, Cummins suggested Australia are considering how different combinations could best suit the conditions."So that's a couple of changes that we've got to match up. What are the conditions going to throw at us? We've got a full squad. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Pat Cummins speaks to Usman Khawaja about autobiography
articles.summary: Pat Cummins confirms he has spoken to Usman Khawaja about his former team-mate’s upcoming autobiography but the Australia captain says he has no concerns about potential sandpapergate revelations.
articles.body:
Pat Cummins has spoken to Usman Khawaja about his former team-mate's upcoming autobiography, but the Australia captain said he has no concerns about potential sandpapergate revelations.

On Friday, Australia will begin their first Test series in South Africa since the ball-tampering scandal erupted in Cape Town in 2018.

At the time, captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and batter Cameron Bancroft were banned for their part in the plot.

Since then, the four Australia bowlers who played in that match, including Cummins, have denied they had any prior knowledge of the plan to cheat.

The quartet, who released a joint statement about the episode in 2021, are once again set to be united in the first Test against South Africa in Durban.

Khawaja played in all four Tests in 2018 and retired from international cricket in January. His autobiography will be released in November.

"Uz gave me a buzz a few weeks back that he is releasing a book," said Cummins. "He didn't go into too much detail, just basically gave me the heads-up that he is doing a book and, as always, no worries.

"Tell your story. It's fine. It's obviously a long time ago and all the investigations, everything was done back then and we answered every question a million times.

"It was dealt with then and all I can say is that as a group, we have moved on and we are very happy with the last eight to nine years how we have been as a group and evolved and obviously my focus is on captaining the cricket team."

At the time of the ball-tampering controversy, Smith explained it was devised by the "leadership group" of the Australian team on the third day of the third Test in Cape Town. Bancroft was caught rubbing sandpaper on the ball the same day.

While Smith, Warner and Bancroft – all batters – were punished, there was never an explanation of how bowlers Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon did not notice a change in the state of the ball.

In a 2021 interview with the Guardian, Bancroft was asked if the bowlers knew and replied: "It's pretty probably self-explanatory."

How an 'absolute fluke' exposed sandpapergate scandal

Test cricket's biggest scandals - your results revealed

Days after Bancroft's interview was published, Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon released their statement which said: "We feel compelled to put the key facts on the record again.

"We did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball until we saw the images on the big screen at Newlands.

"And to those who, despite the absence of evidence, insist that 'we must have known' about the use of a foreign substance simply because we are bowlers, we say this: The umpires during that Test match, Nigel Llong and Richard Illingworth, both very respected and experienced umpires, inspected the ball after the images surfaced on the TV coverage and did not change it because there was no sign of damage.

"We respectfully request an end to the rumour-mongering and innuendo. It has gone on too long and it is time to move on."

Earlier this week, left-arm seamer Starc referenced the scandal when he said: "What's left to come out after eight years?"

And, speaking on Thursday, Cummins said the episode was "a long time ago".

"It's nothing new," the 33-year-old told ABC. "We've spoken about it a little bit. If the crowd gets rowdy or whatever, if someone needs an extra helping hand, we're around.

"To be honest, it's so long ago and we, as a group, move on from things pretty quickly. It hasn't taken up too much of our time."

The trip to South Africa is the first in a year of high-profile away series for Australia. After what appears to be a stern challenge against New Zealand in their home summer, Cummins' men then travel to India and defend the Ashes in England next year.

With all-rounder Cameron Green ruled out because of injury, the tourists are likely to choose between Cooper Connolly and Nic Maddinson for a place in the middle order.

On a Durban pitch expected to turn, South Africa have included two spinners – Keshav Maharaj and Simon Harmer - in their XI.

articles.title: PSL 2027 to clash with IPL again as PCB locks dates; BCCI also eyes early-March start
articles.summary: The Pakistan Super League is heading for another scheduling collision with the Indian Premier League.
articles.body: The Pakistan Super League is heading for another scheduling collision with the Indian Premier League. The Pakistan Cricket Board on Thursday confirmed that PSL 12 will begin on March 18, 2027, and run until May 2, putting the tournament on a potential collision course with IPL 2027 for the second successive season.The eight-team PSL, which expanded from six teams this year, will retain its current format, with the final scheduled for May 2. While the IPL 2027 schedule is yet to be officially announced, indications are that its 20th season could also begin around the middle of March, raising the prospect of the two major T20 leagues once again competing for players, viewers and global attention.IPL-PSL clash looms againThe scheduling overlap could once again create headaches for both leagues, with the IPL also looking at an earlier start in 2027. IPL Governing Council chairman Arun Dhumal had previously indicated that the BCCI was exploring an early-March start, with the aim of completing the tournament by mid-May.“This year, IPL started around March 29 [28], and it was over by May 31,” Saikia told PTI. “Only thing which we are discussing is that during the fag end of the tournament after May 15... there is apprehension of having rainfall or pre-monsoon season starting. On the other hand, there is hot weather which is not very conducive either for the players or for the crowds.“So therefore, there is a discussion going on in BCCI as well as in our IPL governing council regarding whether we can start the tournament a little bit earlier than the fag end of March.“From next year, we will make an effort and I have already instructed our general manager (games development) [former India fast bowler Abey Kuruvilla] to look for the windows, whether we can start it by 10th of March and conclude it by 15th of May. So that there are no adverse weather conditions in the run-up to the playoffs and the finals of IPL 2027, which will be the 20th edition,'' Saikia added.Another season, another IPL-PSL tussleThe scheduling overlap could prove particularly significant after the events of the previous season, when several overseas players withdrew from PSL commitments before joining IPL franchises as replacements.Among them was Australian pacer Spencer Johnson, who had been signed directly by Quetta Gladiators before pulling out, citing personal reasons, and subsequently joining Chennai Super Kings as a replacement for Nathan Ellis.Sri Lanka's Dasun Shanaka, who had been signed by Lahore Qalandars, also joined Rajasthan Royals as a replacement, while Zimbabwe pacer Blessing Muzarabani withdrew from his Islamabad United contract to join Kolkata Knight Riders. Muzarabani was subsequently handed a two-year ban from the PSL.PSL 2027 window lockedThe March 18-May 2 window was finalised following consultations with the franchises and other stakeholders during the PSL Governing Council meeting in London on September 1. The PSL will enter its second season with eight teams, after Hyderabad Kingsmen and the expansion of the competition in 2026. The previous season also marked another major shift, with the traditional player draft replaced by an auction for the first time.Peshawar Zalmi ended a nine-year wait for the PSL title in 2026, defeating debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen in the final at Gaddafi Stadium. The match attracted a record crowd of 32,461.PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi said the league would look to build on the momentum generated by the previous season.“PSL 11 showed the world what this league is capable of, thrilling moments that had the whole nation transfixed, record crowds, record broadcasts,” Naqvi said.“PSL 12 will raise the bar further. articles.title: SA vs AUS, 1st Test: Nortje brings the pace back as South Africa face Australia without Rabada in Durban
articles.summary: WTC champions South Africa will face current World Test Championship points table leaders Australia in Durban on Friday, with the first Test marking the
articles.body: WTC champions South Africa will face current World Test Championship points table leaders Australia in Durban on Friday, with the first Test marking the return of the rivalry to South Africa for the first time since the controversial ‘Sandpapergate’ tour of 2017/18.The 2017/18 series was marked by the Australians being caught using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball. It was also the first time South Africa had beaten Australia in a Test series at home in 48 years.South Africa defeated Australia in the World Test Championship final at Lord’s in London last year, but will enter the series with a slightly inexperienced batting line-up and a depleted fast-bowling attack. Coach Shukri Conrad has described the hamstring injuries affecting his fast bowlers as a “pandemic”.Star fast bowler Kagiso Rabada will miss the first Test at Kingsmead as he continues his recovery from a hamstring injury. South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said Rabada, who took nine wickets when South Africa beat Australia in last year's WTC final at Lord's, would be given more time to recover.Anrich Nortje, however, will return for his first Test since 2023. Bavuma welcomed the return of the 32-year-old, calling him an "X-Factor" player."There are not many guys around bowling at 150kmh plus," Bavuma said at his pre-match press conference.Nortje has had a history of injuries, including back stress fractures, but has been working on his fitness. He played in the European T20 Premier League in the Netherlands and Ireland last month and impressed Bavuma with the pace he produced during South Africa's week-long preparation for the Test.South Africa have selected two specialist spinners in left-arm spinner Keshav Maharaj and off-spinner Simon Harmer. Nortje and Marco Jansen will lead the pace attack, with seam-bowling all-rounder Wiaan Mulder providing support.While Bavuma announced South Africa's playing XI, Australia captain Pat Cummins said the visitors would wait until Friday morning before deciding on their team.Cummins said he was "super-excited" about the series between what he called the "number one and two teams in the world".The series begins a busy 12-month period for Australia, who will also tour India and England for Test series.Cummins said Australia had been good at handling the "big moments" but added that "we need to get better at the grind".He did not reveal the likely make-up of Australia's bowling attack or whether left-arm spinner Matthew Kuhnemann would play alongside off-spinner Nathan Lyon."They definitely could both play," said Cummins. "Kuhnny brings something a little bit different, spinning the ball away from the right-handers. If we need both spinners he's done it well for us in the past."South Africa Team: Aiden Markram, Ryan Rickelton, David Bedingham, Temba Bavuma (captain), Tristan Stubbs, Wiaan Mulder, Kyle Verreynne (wicketkeeper), Marco Jansen, Keshav Maharaj, Simon Harmer, Anrich NortjeStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cowboys guard Tyler Smith set to make his season debut against the Bucs coming off thumb surgery
articles.summary: ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Dallas Cowboys left guard Tyler Smith is set to make his season debut against Tampa Bay on Thursday night after the three-time Pro Bo...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Dallas Cowboys left guard Tyler Smith is set to make his season debut against Tampa Bay on Thursday night after the three-time Pro Bowler was activated coming off left thumb surgery just before the opener .

Smith missed the minimum of four games after going on injured reserve. He sustained ligament damage in his thumb during training camp and tried to play through it. The decision on surgery came the week of Dallas' season-opening 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.

The 25-year-old Smith had been listed as questionable after not getting a chance to participate in a full practice during a short week.

The four games missed are already a career high for Smith, a first-round draft pick in 2022. He played left tackle his entire rookie year after perennial Pro Bowler Tyron Smith was injured in training camp. Smith missed a total of five games over his first four seasons.

The return of Smith puts the entire projected starting lineup on the field together after T.J. Bass filled in for Smith, who is the second-most tenured lineman for Dallas behind right tackle Terence Steele.

The Cowboys waived running back Emari Demercado to make room for Smith on the 53-man roster. Dallas (2-2) also promoted cornerback Reddy Steward and safety Juanyeh Thomas from the practice squad for the meeting with the Bucs.

Steward and Thomas also were brought up from the practice squad for last weekend's 34-30 victory over Houston.

The teenager sent several deliveries sailing towards the stands and the sight screen near the press conference hall.While the senior players went through their practice routines, Sooryavanshi made the most of his time in the nets. The series is scheduled to begin on October 22.Chapman hopes to return for ODIs, Foulkes' recovery timeline unclearChapman suffered a tear in his left hamstring while playing in the European T20 league last month. He is expected to be available for New Zealand's ODI series against India.Foulkes, meanwhile, injured his right hip flexor during a recent Canterbury men's training session.
